annotation.title_clean: Inriktning av ett svenskt regelverk för automatiserad körning inför marknadsintroduktion i obegränsade serier 2027
annotation.title_en: Direction of a Swedish regulatory framework for automated driving ahead of market introduction in unlimited series in 2027
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Lundahl, J.; Andersson, K.; Andersson, J.; Rizgary, D.
annotation.venue: RISE Research Institutes of Sweden & VTI (report commissioned by Transportstyrelsen)
annotation.summary_en: RISE/VTI report for the Swedish Transport Agency analysing the direction of a national regulatory model for automated driving ahead of EU type-approval of unlimited series around 2027. It reviews earlier Swedish proposals and German, French, UK, and other models, and recommends shifting liability from driver to system/organisation, operation rules, trials, and monitoring.
key_provisions_or_claims: National traffic, liability and use rules are needed alongside EU type-approval; unclear liability is the main barrier.
SOU 2018:16 and Ds 2021:28 remain largely relevant; limited driver liability and system/organisational liability endorsed.
Consider operation or authorisation rules for automated transport services, drawing on German, French and UK models.
Keep and develop the trial regulation as an intermediate step, including remote operation and role handover.
Do not allow remote SAE level 3 operation until technical approval rules exist; address cybersecurity, cross-border enforcement and insurance.
